scores.evidence: Steps with expected results, prompt cards with fill-in fields, the practice-checklist and the 4-node practice-flow diagram all render cleanly. The diagram is readable at 390 px (mobile-jp-11) and in EN (desktop-en-08). On desktop the diagram is a narrow vertical strip in a wide, mostly empty card. It also follows the practice-tip callout with no sentence introducing it.

No screen is text-only (textOnlyScreens is empty on all three runs). Desktop JP median is 36 chars per line (target 30-40) and EN median is 70 (target 60-75). Prose stays at 2-4 lines between components, and there are no walls of text in the full-length captures.

The EN run is fully translated, including prompts, the checklist, diagram node labels and flashcards, and no Japanese is left in desktop-en-*. The diagram has a caption and a 'Describe the figure in words' / 図の説明を読む disclosure. Quizzes show keyboard hints, and nothing is hidden under the mobile top or bottom bars.

niceToHave: practice-flow: add one sentence before the diagram, e.g. 「図1は、出欠確認アプリのMustだけで目的を最後まで果たせるかを示した例です。」. Right now it follows the practice-tip callout with no lead-in (desktop-jp-07/08, mobile-jp-11).
practice-flow: on desktop the 4-node TD chart sits in a wide card that is mostly empty (desktop-jp-07/08). That is acceptable, but keep TD for mobile and do not switch to LR.
reader: the flashcard hint says 「クリックまたはスペースキーでめくる」 even on the 390 px mobile view (mobile-jp-18). On touch devices it should say タップ.

reader: the end banner says 「このコースの最後のレッスンまで読み終えました」 because the draft is not listed in course.json, while summary-next points ahead to 第3章 (mobile-jp-19, desktop-jp-13). In preview, the banner should not claim this is the last lesson.
reader: on mobile, the step header 「自分で分けて、AIに見直してもらう」 runs right up to the 完了 checkbox (mobile-jp-07). The reader should reserve a little gap or let the title wrap earlier.
summary: The metrics are clean: no overflow or console, mermaid, block or image errors, and characters per line are on target in JP and EN. The lesson reads as a well-paced sequence of steps, prompt cards, checklist and quizzes on both mobile and desktop. The only lesson-side suggestion is a lead-in sentence for the practice-flow diagram. The other notes are reader issues.
